'''2011 World Championship''' was the 16th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] in Washington, D.C., on 11–14 August 2011.<ref name="forum" /><ref name="awards" /> The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Virtual Block 7.3]]. 63 players took part.<ref name="wp" /> [[Kevin Shannon]], the sixth seed, defeated [[Brian Herold]] in the final, playing Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi (V) and Heading For The Medical Frigate on Day 3.<ref name="f75427-1300387">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300387#p1300387 Post by Yoshi], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1300387 Internet Archive]</ref> He was the second player, after [[Jonny Chu]], to win two World Championships (2008 and 2011).<ref name="awards" /> The Players Committee published the Day 2 and Day 3 decklists; no Day 1 or Team Tournament lists were published.<ref name="decklists">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2011-decklists/ 2011 Decklists], starwarsccg.org</ref>

Day 2 decklist sheets are in [[:File:2011 Worlds Day 2.pdf]] (121 pages). Three sheets carry no player name. They are published as ''Unknown player'' decks, named by PDF page (see [[#Other published decklists|Other published decklists]]): p39 Dark Kessel, p120 Light Coruscant: Night Club and p121 Light Watch Your Step. Josh Mack's Day 2 Dark Side sheet (p78) reads ''Same As Day 1'', and no Day 1 lists were published. His Light Side deck was Communing (Speeder Bowl XL).
